title: Cross-account GPU VPC mesh and per-tenant NAT scaling
author: Asha Menon
body:
Overview:

Purpose
This document describes the architecture, Terraform/IaC patterns, CI/CD gating, and operational runbook for a cross-account GPU VPC mesh with per-tenant NAT scaling ("nat-scaler") to avoid SNAT port exhaustion, reduce egress cost spikes, and provide predictable egress SLAs for Dedicated and Private customers. It captures the recommended modules, ownership, rollout steps, monitoring, and troubleshooting guidance.

Scope
- Applies to all multi-tenant GPU clusters that require cross-account networking (Shared VPCs, Partner accounts, customer-dedicated VPCs)
- Covers AWS and GCP patterns we maintain today; Azure guidance is in the appendix
- Does NOT cover application-layer proxying (eg: per-tenant outbound proxies for content filtering) — this focuses on egress NAT scale and mesh networking.

Background and motivation
Redwood operates heterogeneous GPU pools across many accounts and projects. When tenants burst (large evals, nightly batch evals, or model warmups) we observe SNAT port exhaustion, asymmetric egress costs across accounts, and fragile cross-account routing during node churn. The nat-scaler + vpc-mesh approach provides:
- Elastic SNAT capacity per-tenant with predictable thresholds
- Multipath egress routing for cost-aware failover (prefer spot egress gateway -> reserved gateway)
- Terraform modules for a reproducible cross-account deployment pattern

Architecture overview
The high-level components are:
- egress-mesh-controller (K8s controller in control plane account): reconciles mesh attachments, routes, and policies
- tenant-egress-gateway (lightweight EC2/GCE autoscaled pool or EKS nodegroup): handles centralized SNAT and egress policy for a tenant/account
- nat-scaler (serverless autoscaler that manages number of gateway instances and NAT port pools per tenant)
- egress-proxy (optional HTTP(S) / SOCKS proxy for content-level rules)
- terraform modules: networking/gateway, mesh-attachment, nat-shim, iam-bindings

ASCII diagram (textual):

  [Tenant VPC A] -- VPC-Peering/Transit -> [Shared Egress VPC] <- Transit/VPN -> [Tenant VPC B]
                       |
                       |-- autoscaling tenant-egress-gateway pool (SNAT)
                       |-- nat-scaler (manages port pools and instance counts)
                       |-- egress-mesh-controller (applies routing & fallbacks)

Service-level objectives and thresholds
- Egress availability (gateway reachable and able to allocate ports): 99.9% (monthly)
- SNAT port exhaustion events (per-tenant): target < 1 per quarter
- Failover time between preferred and fallback egress path: < 30s (automated routing cutover)
- 95th percentile egress path latency (measurement at proxy sidecar): < 120ms for regional traffic

Terraform / IaC modules and patterns
We follow a split-control pattern: networking resources live in the Shared-Network account; tenant attachments and minimal IAM live in tenant accounts. Use the following modules:
- module.networking/egress-vpc (creates shared NAT gateways, Transit Gateway attachments)
- module.networking/tenant-attachment (per-tenant VPC attachment & route propagation)
- module.runtime/tenant-egress-gateway (autoscaling ASG/InstanceGroup with bootstrapped nat-agent)
- module.runtime/nat-shim (lambda/fn + DynamoDB/GCS state for port pool accounting)
- module.iam/mesh-bindings (cross-account IAM roles + trust policies)

Example Terraform usage (simplified):

// Tenant account: attach to shared egress VPC
module "tenant-attachment" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-infra/terraform//modules/tenant-attachment"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  shared_network_account = var.shared_network_account
  routes = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

// Shared network: create gateway pool for tenant region
module "gateway-pool" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-infra/terraform//modules/tenant-egress-gateway"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  instance_type = "c6i.large"
  min_size = 1
  max_size = 8
  nat_agent_bootstrap_script = file("./bootstrap/nat-agent.sh")
}

Key IaC design constraints
- Immutable infra: instances boot with signed runtime bundles; upgrades via image rotation and controlled ASG rollouts
- Cross-account secrets: use short-lived assume-role (AWS STS) or Workload Identity (GCP) rather than long-lived credentials in Terraform state
- State partitioning: one Terraform workspace per-tenant-attachment to reduce blast radius

CI/CD and gating
- All modules live in infra-modules monorepo. Merges require: 
  1) unit tests & tfsec linting (pre-commit)
  2) plan in ephemeral tenant workspace with synthetic tenant (ci-tenant-0001)
  3) integration test that deploys minimal gateway in sandbox account and runs e2e connectivity checks
- Promotion to production (shared-network account) is gated on: green e2e, manual approval by network-owners team, and a DB migration safety-check for nat-shim port tables
- Rollout pattern: canary to 5 tenants -> 25 tenants -> full rollout. Each canary run must be observed for 48 hours before next phase.

Operational runbook: common incidents and playbooks
1) SNAT port exhaustion detected for tenant X
   - Symptoms: increased 502/504 in telemetry, Prometheus alert NAT_PORT_EXHAUSTION{tenant="X"} fired, flow logs show excessive ephemeral port usage
   - Immediate action (automated): nat-scaler increases gateway ASG by factor 2, allocate new port pools in nat-shim; notify oncall
   - Manual action if automated fails:
     a) kubectl -n infra describe nat-shim tenant-X -> inspect allocation state
     b) aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name tenant-X-gw-asg --desired-capacity 4
     c) If ports still exhausted: enable per-tenant egress-throttling policy in egress-mesh-controller (rate-limit outbound flows to 10k ports/min)
   - Postmortem checklist: collect flow logs (5 min before to 30 min after), nat-shim allocation history, and schedule quota-smoothing with product for tenant X.

2) Egress mesh route flap between shared-network and tenant account
   - Symptoms: asymmetric routing, packet drops, > 1% 5xx across dependent services
   - Quick checks: verify Transit Gateway attachments, BGP state (if using TGW), route tables propagation, and egress-mesh-controller logs
   - Temporary mitigation: switch affected tenant to fallback egress path (egress-mesh-controller "force-fallback" API)
   - Long term: apply route propagation hardening with static fallback routes and health probes.

Monitoring, telemetry and dashboards
- Metrics to instrument:
  - nat_shim.ports_allocated{tenant}
  - nat_shim.ports_free{tenant}
  - gateway_pool.cpu_utilization, gateway_pool.network_bytes_in/out
  - egress_mesh.path_health{preferred|fallback}
  - per-tenant egress_cost_rate (daily burn)
- Alerts (prometheus):
  - NAT_PORT_EXHAUSTION: ports_free < 50 for 5m -> severity P0
  - EGRESS_POOL_CPU_HIGH: avg_cpu > 80% for 10m -> P1
  - ROUTE_PROPAGATION_FAIL: missing route probes > 3 -> P1
- Dashboards: tenant-level egress capacity (ports, instances), cross-account cost heatmap, and per-region failover latency. Default Grafana folder: "Infra / Egress Mesh"

Security and compliance notes
- Network audit logs and flow logs must be retained for 90 days for Dedicated customers and 365 days for regulated customers (per compliance package).
- IAM role usage: cross-account assume-role is audited; terraform runs that mutate shared-network must be performed from CI runner with short-lived tokens.
- Encryption: nat-shim state in DynamoDB/GCS must be encrypted-at-rest and only accessible to nat-shim roles.

Troubleshooting playbook (quick commands)
- Check nat-shim allocation: kubectl -n infra logs deployment/nat-shim --tail=200 | grep tenant-X
- List ASG instances (AWS): aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Tenant,Values=tenant-X" --query "Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,PrivateIpAddress,State.Name]"
- Verify route propagation (GCP example): gcloud compute routes list --filter="name~tenant-x"

Rollback and rollback criteria
- Rollback triggers:
  - >5% production traffic errors attributable to new gateway change
  - repeated SNAT exhaustion post-deploy
  - security policy violation detected in nat-shim changes
- Rollback steps:
  1) Revert Terraform to previous module version in infra-modules monorepo
  2) Redeploy shared-network plan into sandbox for validation (must pass connectivity smoke tests)
  3) Apply to production and verify canary tenants

Ownership and contacts
- Network owners: infra-networking@redwood.com (primary oncall rotation)
- Module owners: terraform-modules-team (owners listed in module README)
- Oncall escalation: follow standard eng-infra escalation matrix (see /confluence/eng-infra/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process)

Appendix A: GCP specifics
- GCP uses Cloud NAT with per-router port allocation; nat-scaler instead adjusts number of Cloud NAT VM attachments or configures multiple Cloud NATs per tenant with evenly partitioned port ranges.
- Service names: egress-mesh-controller -> GKE controller; nat-shim -> Cloud Function backed by Firestore state.

Appendix B: Example nat-shim state schema (YAML sample)
- tenant: tenant-X
- allocated_pools:
  - pool_id: tcp-pool-01
    ports_start: 32768
    ports_end: 39999
    allocated: 1200
  - pool_id: tcp-pool-02
    ports_start: 40000
    ports_end: 46200
    allocated: 40

Appendix C: Change log
- 2024-05-03: initial draft and prototype Terraform modules defined.
- 2024-11-21: nat-scaler automated scaling added; initial canary to 3 tenants.
- 2025-08-30: CI/CD gating tightened; require DB safety-checks before shared-network promotion.
- 2025-11-12: Added AWS/GCP parity notes and updated SLOs.

Related pages and references:
- module README links are in the infra-modules monorepo: https://git.redwood.com/infra-modules/tenant-egress-gateway
- Egress billing playbook: /confluence/eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/egress-billing-clarity-and-multipath-metering-spec.json

Contact and next steps
- To request a canary slot for a tenant, open an internal ticket to infra-networking and include tenant id, expected burst profile (tokens/sec, concurrent connections), and required retention window for flow logs.
- Roadmap: automate per-tenant cost caps and incorporate model-level throttles into egress-mesh-controller (Q2 2026).

End of document.
